title: Sunny and the Shooting Star | Bedtime Story
description: Join Sunny the Quokka on a magical evening walk under the night sky in this gentle bedtime story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories. Sunny lies down in a moonlit clearing and watches in wonder as a shooting star streaks silently across the darkness.
narration:
The bush was soft and still tonight. Little Sunny the quokka padded quietly along the path, her golden paws gentle on the cool, mossy ground. The trees leaned overhead, their leaves whispering. The stars were beginning to blink awake, one by one.

Sunny found a clearing — a small, round patch of open sky. She lay down on a cushion of sweet grass and looked up. The sky was deep and dark and full of tiny lights. She could feel the earth warm beneath her tummy.

She counted one star. Then two. Then she stopped counting, because there were too many, and that made her smile.

Then — oh.

A streak of silver light rushed across the sky. So quick. So quiet. A shooting star, trailing a soft silver ribbon behind it, melting into the dark.

Sunny breathed in slowly. She had never seen anything so beautiful and so fast. It was there, and then it was gone, like a tiny sigh from the sky.

She lay very still, her round eyes soft and warm. Maybe another one would come. Maybe not. Either way, the sky was still full of so many gentle lights, watching over the bush, watching over her.

Sunny's paws curled in. Her eyes grew heavy. The grass was so soft. The night was so quiet. She let her eyes close, still smiling.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, shooting star. Goodnight, little one.
